title: From 2D Grids to 1D Tokens: Reforming Shared Representations for Multimodal Image Fusion
claim: Prior shared representations entangle global appearance with local detail on a grid; ours centralizes global appearance in a few tokens, decoupled from spatial detail.
layout: 2 stacked panels, top-to-bottom, (a) prior vs (b) ours, color-coded backgrounds
description: Two stacked rounded panels. The top panel (a), on a gray background, shows a stack of 2D feature-map grids with a yellow glow spread across many cells to depict global appearance. Texture patches sit in individual cells. Arrows link the grid to the labels 'Base (global appearance): distributed' and 'Detail (local structures)'. A red warning box reads 'Hard to regulate global appearance: base is spatially entangled'. A formula box gives I_f = D(F) and F = E_2D(I_x, I_y). The bottom panel (b), on a teal background, shows a row of icon-labeled base tokens and a dashed row of aux/residual tokens. An arrow carries the tokens through π(·) to a glowing base map B. The base map is added (⊕) to a black 3D detail-map grid D, and the sum feeds a decoder that outputs I_f. Side notes read 'easier to steer' and 'decoupled control'.
caption: {2D grids vs. 1D tokens for base/detail decoupling in multimodal image fusion.} (a) A 2D shared feature map entangles global base appearance with local details. (b) We represent base in a compact 1D token set $Z$, map it to a base map via $\pi(\cdot)$, and combine it with a spatial detail map $D$ for decoding.
abstract: Multimodal image fusion aims to integrate complementary information from different modalities into a fused image that preserves rich local details while maintaining globally consistent appearance. Existing approaches build shared representations on 2D feature grids, which excel at modeling local structures but offer limited leverage over image-level global appearance factors. To balance these objectives, we introduce a compact 1D token interface based on a frozen pretrained image tokenizer for modeling non-local appearance/base factors. Rather than using the tokenizer as a reconstruction backbone, our design uses the 1D token space as a global carrier while retaining the 2D spatial pathway for local structure restoration. Specifically, we introduce Selective Token Editing (STE), which sparsely updates/replaces a small set of critical tokens, providing a lightweight mechanism to steer global appearance coherence while keeping the fusion backbone unchanged and avoiding extra losses. Experiments on four commonly used benchmarks show that our method achieves the best overall performance, with consistent, multi-metric improvements in both global coherence and local fidelity. Project page: https://zju-xyc.github.io/1D-Fusion-Project-Page/
